think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 32-year-old immunocompetent, HIV-negative woman living in Guangdong Province presents acutely with dyspnea, chest pain, and sinus tachycardia, found to have a large (4.0 × 3.6 cm) middle mediastinal mass compressing the lower trachea and superior vena cava with right middle lobe infiltration. This acute mass effect in an immunocompetent young patient strongly suggests an aggressive malignant mediastinal neoplasm (such as lymphoma or thymic carcinoma) or acute bacterial mediastinitis.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Initial admission evaluation and contrast-enhanced chest CT showing the middle mediastinal mass (4.0 × 3.6 cm) causing extrinsic compression of the lower trachea and SVC with intramediastinal adenopathy and right middle lobe infiltration, prior to Day 4 bronchoscopy, EBUS-TBNA, mNGS, fungal cultures, and biopsy histopathology.
3. Differential Distinctions: Malignant mediastinal neoplasm (lymphoma / thymic tumor) was the primary concern due to the rapidly compressing middle mediastinal mass, but ruled out by EBUS-TBNA and biopsy showing no tumor cells. Tuberculous mediastinal lymphadenitis was considered given positive T-SPOT in an endemic area, but ruled out by negative acid-fast stains and isolation of a dimorphic fungus. Acute bacterial mediastinitis was initially suspected due to leukocytosis and elevated procalcitonin, but broad-spectrum antibiotics (moxifloxacin) were ineffective.
case_prompt: A 32-year-old woman residing in Guangdong Province, China, presents with acute-onset dyspnea and chest pain of four days' duration, accompanied by cough productive of small amounts of sputum and occasional low-grade fever. She denies night sweats, hemoptysis, weight loss, rash, or joint swelling. Her medical history includes hypotension, hypoglycemia, bile reflux gastritis, asymptomatic hepatitis B virus carriage, and an interventional procedure for spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage at age 20 without residual neurological deficit. She is a lifelong non-smoker with no history of recent travel, wild animal contacts, or sick contacts. On physical examination, her blood pressure is 92/65 mmHg, heart rate is 122 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 21 breaths per minute, body temperature is 99.7°F (37.6°C), and oxygen saturation is 95% on room air. Chest auscultation reveals coarse breath sounds bilaterally without wheezes or crackles. Laboratory testing shows a leukocyte count of 14,360 cells/mm^3 with 10,820 neutrophils/mm^3, 1,960 lymphocytes/mm^3, and 850 monocytes/mm^3. Procalcitonin is elevated at 0.594 ng/mL (normal: <0.1 ng/mL). Blood gas analysis, cardiac enzymes, NT-proBNP, D-dimer, and baseline serum chemistries are normal. Serum IgG is slightly elevated at 20.8 g/L (normal: 8.6–17.4 g/L). HIV antibody testing, autoimmune panels, and tumor markers are negative. Sputum culture and electrocardiogram show no obvious abnormalities. Initial chest radiograph indicates bilateral pneumonia. Contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography (CT) reveals a 4.0 × 3.6 cm non-uniformly enhancing middle mediastinal mass causing severe extrinsic compression of the lower trachea and superior vena cava, with enlarged intramediastinal lymph nodes and right middle lobe infiltration.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Malignant Mediastinal Neoplasm (Lymphoma vs. Thymic Carcinoma)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The acute middle mediastinal mass causing severe tracheal stenosis and superior vena cava compression in a young adult strongly raised suspicion of lymphoma or thymic neoplasm, but multiple biopsies demonstrated inflammatory changes without tumor cells.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: TBLB showed acute inflammation, negative for Acid-fast, PAS and GMS stains, and no tumor cells were seen (Figure 3A).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: T-SPOT testing was positive, which raised suspicion of tuberculous lymphadenitis in an endemic setting; however, acid-fast stains of lung tissue and needle aspirates were negative, and fungal cultures confirmed a dimorphic mold.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: T-Spot test suggested positive while other blood tests showed negative for blood culture, cryptococcal antigen latex agglutination test, candida galactomannan antigen test, (1-3)-beta-D glucan antigen test, tumor-associated antigens and HIV antibodies.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) yielded specimens that grew characteristic red-pigmented fungal colonies on Sabouraud dextrose agar at 25°C, with histopathology revealing yeast cells with characteristic transverse septa on PAS and GMS staining.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: On the 9th day of admission, culturing on Sabouraud dextrose agar medium at 25 C confirmed T. marneffei in the biopsied mass with colonies showing characteristic red-pigmented fungal colonies from the needle aspirates (Figure 2D).

editor_comments: Distilled from PMC9692072. Admission narrative excludes bronchoscopic findings, EBUS needle aspirate culture, mNGS, and fungal histology.
